summary: Initial discovery for residency and evidence needs. Stormvale Health is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PHI workloads. Key constraints: keys must be in-country for EU patients, audit log redaction/retention policies, BAA required, pen-test and attestation workflow, and latency tradeoffs for on-prem. Redwood AE + SE outlined Hosted fallbacks, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM options and audit log controls. Agreed pilot timeline and deliverables.
topics: Residency requirements (EU patient data vs US)
Key management: KMS vs HSM, in-country keys
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Pen-test, SOC2 evidence, and procurement timeline
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09 15:00 PT
Duration: ~57 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Head of Data, Stormvale), Marcus Yu (CISO), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you taking the time. Quick intros — I work with enterprise healthcare accounts focusing on hosting and compliance. Jonas is our systems engineer.
[00:12] Dr. Lena: Hi all, Lena here. We're trying to map how we can put patient-facing NLP into our triage product, need to understand data residency and audit paths.
[00:18] Marcus: Marcus — security. Main ask: no unintended egress of PHI, keys in-country for EU, and clear audit logs for regulatory review.
[00:26] Priya: Priya, infra — we'll be assessing latency impact and integration with our KMS + HSMs.
[00:33] Maya: Great, so high level we'll run quickly through hosting options: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private (VPC / on-prem). We'll call out control plane, data plane separation, key residency, and logging.
[00:45] Jonas: One note — sometimes in transcripts you'll see 'K-V cache' or similar; we meant KV cache for context storage and prefix caching.
[00:52] Dr. Lena: Right, we have strict GDPR obligations for EU patients. Any patient data that leaves EU is a no-go unless it's pseudonymized. We also need a record of every inference that touched PHI for audit sampling.
[01:05] Maya: Understood. For Hosted, we can restrict routing to EU-only regions and redwood's hosted catalog has EU endpoints. However, Hosted still has a shared control plane unless you opt for Private where control plane is customer-managed.
[01:18] Marcus: So with Hosted — even if region is EU, what about keys? We need keys resident in EU, not Redwood-managed KMS in US.
[01:26] Jonas: Good question — Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. We offer Dedicated with customer-managed KMS via Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) in some tiers, and Private gives you full control — you can provision HSM-backed keys inside your VPC or on-prem HSM. There are steps for key escrow and rotation.
[01:38] Priya: If we go Private VPC, is the control plane still with Redwood? We need the option for private control plane because procurement won't allow our metadata to leave the tenancy.
[01:47] Maya: Yes, we have a Private offering with a private control plane option — can be deployed into your cloud account or in an on-prem bundle. That addresses metadata residency.
[01:54] Dr. Lena: Audit logs — what granularity do the logs have? We need request-level logs that include model version, timestamp, and a hashed token to link back to our internal IDs, but we cannot have raw PHI in logs.
[02:05] Jonas: Redwood can provide structured audit logs with configurable redaction. Options: full logs (useful for debugging), redacted logs (strip prompt/response), or tokenized references. We can also stream logs to customer-owned S3 or Kafka in-region.
[02:18] Marcus: Do you support deterministic redaction or regex-based PII scrubbing? We run our own PII scrubber before sending, but want to ensure logs stored by Redwood don't have leftovers.
[02:27] Jonas: We support a configurable log pipeline — you can opt for server-side redaction rules, and we also recommend client-side scrubbers as defense in depth. We'll share sample redaction configs.
[02:36] Dr. Lena: About BAAs — do you sign BAAs and what is the scope? We need assurance on subcontractors and log access.
[02:44] Maya: We do sign BAAs for healthcare customers. The typical BAA covers data processing, subcontractor flow-downs, and breach notification terms. We'll send a standard template but procurement often redlines it.
[02:54] Marcus: Penetration testing — will Redwood support external pentest requests or provide attestation?
[03:00] Jonas: For Dedicated/Private, customers can request pentesting against their private endpoints; for Hosted we provide our SOC2 and penetration test summaries. For private/on-prem installations we can provide more targeted support.
[03:10] Priya: What's the expected latency penalty for Private on-prem vs Hosted? Our triage UX needs sub-200ms median token latency for short prompts.
[03:19] Jonas: Latency depends on proximity to model shards — Hosted in-region is fastest; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency; Private on-prem offers best locality but depends on your hardware. For small short prompts the difference might be 20-50ms if on-prem is colocated with app.
[03:33] Maya: Also tradeoffs around autoscaling — Dedicated has reserved pools and burst options to prevent cold starts; Private requires you to size capacity or use our private autoscaler if you want.
[03:42] Dr. Lena: Regarding evidence: regulators will ask for an audit trail showing where data was processed and who accessed logs. Can that be exported for, say, a 3rd party audit?
[03:51] Jonas: Yes, we can export audit artifacts including deployment manifests, key rotation logs, and request-level metadata (subject to redaction configs). Exports can be signed and delivered to your storage.
[04:02] Marcus: One subtlety — if you stream logs to our S3 bucket in EU, how do we prove non-modification of logs? We need integrity proofs.
[04:10] Jonas: We support signed log exports and can include hash chains or S3 versioning + signed manifests so you can verify tamper-evidence. We'll provide the export spec.
[04:20] Priya: For KMS, we need to attach our HSM-backed keys. Do you have integrations with cloud KMS providers and common HSM vendors?
[04:28] Maya: Yes — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP CMEK are supported for Dedicated and Private. For on-prem HSMs we integrate via PKCS#11 or by bringing a gateway. We also support custom key escrow policies.
[04:41] Dr. Lena: What about model outputs stored temporarily for caching? Where is the KV cache kept and for how long?
[04:48] Jonas: The KV cache is in-memory for inference nodes and can be disabled or configured to persist to customer-controlled storage. Default caching TTLs are short (minutes) but are configurable per workload. We can also disable persistent caching for PHI paths.
[05:00] Marcus: Ok, procurement constraints: must be SOC2 Type II, BAA, keys not exported from EU region for EU data, log retention configurable down to 30 days with archiving to cold storage, and pen-test attestation. Timeline wise, we aim to start a pilot in July and put into production Q4.
[05:16] Maya: That timeline is workable — pilot in July matches our capacity. We'll propose a Dedicated pilot with EU-only residency and a Private option on the table if procurement blocks hosted.
[05:27] Dr. Lena: Are there any differences in model behavior or versioning across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? We need deterministic model versions for validation.
[05:36] Jonas: Model binaries are the same across modes — you can pin versions and we support rollout policies for canaries and A/B tests. For Private you host the same verified artifacts. There can be minor performance differences due to quantization or kernel selection across hardware. We'll include a performance profile.
[05:49] Priya: For the audit artifacts, is there a common format? Our GRC team wants CSV/JSON exports and an SSO-backed access log to show who retrieved them.
[05:58] Jonas: Exports can be JSON or CSV, and we support SAML-based audit access with RBAC. We can include retrieval logs in the evidence package.
[06:07] Speaker 1 (crosstalk): ummm, yeah —
[06:09] Marcus: One more on redaction: if there's a failure in redaction path, how do you alert us?
[06:15] Jonas: We have alerting hooks and can send webhook events to your security ops when redaction rules trigger errors; plus we maintain counters for failed redactions in our telemetry.
[06:25] Dr. Lena: For EU residency, do you support geo-fencing of backups and snapshots? We need guarantees that snapshots of model caches or logs won't cross borders.
[06:34] Maya: Yes, region-locking for backups is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region options but backups are handled per our retention policy; for strict geofence you'd want Private with customer-managed storage.
[06:46] Priya: How does cost scale? Dedicated with two regional pools + EU KMS BYOK — ballpark?
[06:54] Maya: We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up. For pilots we often do a short discount to validate throughput.
[07:01] Marcus: Ok. Procurement will also run vendor risk — do you provide an attestation package or a security questionnaire?
[07:08] Jonas: We provide our security package, SOC2 report, penetration test summary, and a pre-filled vendor questionnaire (SIG-lite). We can help iterate on that.
[07:18] Dr. Lena: There's one last thing — our legal asked about subcontractor access: will Redwood staff ever see unredacted PHI?
[07:25] Maya: By default Redwood engineers won't access customer data; support access can be configured with strict controls and require explicit approval and will be logged. For Hosted, support access is controlled and audited; for Private you can completely restrict Redwood access.
[07:38] Priya: Any known blockers we've seen from other health customers?
[07:42] Jonas: Mostly it's procurement and the BAA negotiation, plus KMS residency logistics. Technical integration tends to be straightforward once keys and logs are agreed.
[07:49] Maya: Next steps recap — we'll send the SOC2/HIPAA packet and BAA, Jonas will send network and KMS flow diagrams, and we'll propose pilot SKUs and dates.
[07:58] Marcus: Sounds good. Looking forward to the docs.
[08:02] Dr. Lena: Thanks everyone.

End recap (automated notes):
- Pilot: Dedicated EU + US pools proposed; Private on-prem if procurement requires.
- Controls: BYOK/HSM integration, in-region key residency, configurable redaction and audit log export, SSO/RBAC for access to audit artifacts.
- Deliverables: SOC2/HIPAA docs, network diagram, export spec, cost estimate.
